# Vendored Yuxi source

Source: https://github.com/xerrors/Yuxi

Version: `v0.7.3`

Commit: `caff3208c9db9128aa0b277bc5c669141383ddbd`

The Python source under `package/yuxi/knowledge` (62 files), `package/yuxi/models` (10 files), and `package/yuxi/permissions` (2 files) is vendored from the local upstream checkout. A SHA-256 comparison against the recorded v0.7.3 commit found 59/62 knowledge files, 10/10 model files, and 2/2 permission files identical; three knowledge files have small local patches. Dify and Notion re-raise upstream request failures instead of returning an indistinguishable empty result, and knowledge implementation classes load lazily so using read-only connectors does not import the optional Milvus client. Geo RAG Studio actively calls the upstream Dify and Notion connectors, `OtherEmbedding`, chunk parsers, OCR parser classes, reranker wire protocols, provider templates, and retrieval evaluation metrics through local adapters. The external knowledge-base API also calls Yuxi's `KnowledgeBase.build_search_output`, `_build_open_file_window`, and `_build_find_file_windows` helpers directly, together with the upstream content-hash helper for duplicate upload rejection; local SQLite metadata and parsed blocks supply the source data. The chunk adapter adds PDF source-location metadata and validates knowledge-base chunk settings. Local MinIO and Redis shims report those optional services unavailable; provider credentials remain in the SQLite registry.

Geo RAG's FastAPI routes in `app/yuxi_compat.py` are local adapters, not verbatim copies of Yuxi's `backend/server/routers` modules. A method-and-path comparison against Yuxi v0.7.3's knowledge, external knowledge, evaluation, graph, and knowledge-dashboard routers found all 77 operations represented. This verifies route surface only; it does not establish equivalent behavior for every operation.

The document lifecycle now calls the vendored `resolve_processing_params` and `params_for_uploaded_document` helpers directly. Per-request parameters override stored file parameters, which override knowledge-base defaults; effective chunk settings and OCR selection are persisted with the document. Reindexing without parameters retains the file settings, while `index-pending` forwards its native frontend parameters. The upload-only `documents/add` endpoint preserves `uploaded` status without parsing or indexing and returns Yuxi's `items`, `failed_items`, `added`, `failed`, and partial-failure contract. Parsing and indexing remain separate operations. Geo currently executes those operations synchronously rather than through Yuxi's task queue; queued task behavior is still a parity gap.

On 2026-10-03, the Python suite passed 81 tests and compilation passed. A real 1,528,947-byte, 49-page PDF was uploaded, parsed and indexed through the authenticated Java `:8007` gateway to RAG `:8010`. Its knowledge-base default remained 512 tokens while a file override of 256 tokens / 0% overlap produced 67 chunks; all 67 chunk texts matched a direct call to the vendored Yuxi dispatcher. Reindexing without overrides also produced 67 chunks. Keyword retrieval returned 50 BM25 candidates and five final evidences with 1,840 context characters. All five page/bbox pairs matched stored source spans and contained text within the actual PDF. This proves the tested lifecycle and configuration behavior, not complete knowledge-base parity. Embedding, Reranker and MinerU provider probes returned HTTP 503 `unavailable` because their services/credentials were not configured; the local PyMuPDF probe returned 49 pages and 1,008 blocks with bboxes.

To complete the vendored knowledge package's internal source dependencies, 25 supporting Python files were copied unchanged from the same Yuxi checkout: configuration, repositories, OCR/task services, MinIO/Postgres/Neo4j adapters, and utilities. SHA-256 hashes matched the upstream working tree after copying. The Geo-local MinIO import shim remains active in place of Yuxi's service-bound package initializer, while exposing the migrated MinIO client modules as optional submodules. The upstream `MilvusKB` class is vendored and importable but is not the active Geo pipeline class: its indexing lifecycle uses Yuxi's PostgreSQL file/chunk repositories, model registry, and MinIO-backed parsed files. Geo instead keeps source files, parsed blocks, chunk metadata, and provider configuration in its own local SQLite/filesystem layer and calls a Geo-owned Milvus adapter when `RAG_SEARCH_BACKEND=milvus`.

Parser files are from the same v0.7.3 source commit. OCR integrations use the upstream RapidOCR, MinerU, PP-Structure, DeepSeek OCR, and PaddleOCR classes when their required local packages, endpoints, credentials, and (where relevant) image storage support are present. Missing providers are reported as unavailable; no parser result is synthesized.

License: MIT, copied from the upstream root `LICENSE` file in this directory.

The active Geo pipeline selects its index with `RAG_SEARCH_BACKEND`: `sqlite` uses the local BM25/vector fallback, while `milvus` writes and retrieves chunks from a project-owned Milvus collection. The active Milvus adapter uses the same Chinese analyzer, BM25 Function, COSINE vector metric, IVF_FLAT vector index, sparse DAAT_MAXSCORE index, query parameters, and Milvus 2.5.6 `WeightedRanker` as Yuxi. It adds Geo-specific per-knowledge-base hashed collection names and a `has_embedding` filter so BM25-only documents can coexist with embedded chunks. Geo's separate SQLite document/chunk metadata remains the source for evidence text, page/bbox spans, and local file filters. The active code is therefore behavior-aligned at the Milvus query layer, but is not a direct runtime invocation of Yuxi's `MilvusKB` class. We have not established full functional parity for every Yuxi knowledge-base operation or identical ranking against the live Yuxi service; PostgreSQL, Redis, Neo4j, and Yuxi's Docker harness have not been reintroduced.
